blocks.content: FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Fundamental Duties are moral and civic obligations of Indian citizens located in Part IVA, Article 51A.
Added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inspired by the former USSR constitution.
Originally 10 in number, the 11th duty (providing education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and apply only to citizens, serving to promote discipline, patriotism, and national integrity.
Although non-justiciable directly, courts use them to interpret laws, evaluate constitutional validity, and support enforcement through specific acts like the Environment Protection Act.
INTRODUCTION

blocks.content: Fundamental Duties are the moral and civic obligations of citizens towards the nation. They remind citizens that along with rights, they also have certain responsibilities to perform.
Fundamental Duties are mentioned in Part IVA of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A. They were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.
ORIGIN AND BACKGROUND OF FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES
The concept of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR (Soviet Union).
Initially, the Indian Constitution did not contain Fundamental Duties.
They were added on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976).
The main purpose of adding Fundamental Duties was:

items:
• To promote discipline and patriotism
  • To remind citizens of their responsibilities
  • To strengthen national unity and integrity
To promote discipline and patriotism
To remind citizens of their responsibilities
To strengthen national unity and integrity

blocks.content: ARTICLE 51A – FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES
Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
Originally, 10 Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
Later, the 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
LIST OF FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES
The Fundamental Duties are as follows:

items: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired the freedom struggle.
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.
To defend the country and render national service when called upon.
To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood.
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
To protect and improve the natural environment.
To develop scientific temper, humanism and spirit of inquiry.
To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
To provide opportunities for education to children between 6–14 years (added by 86th Amendment).

blocks.content: FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES AND FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS
Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties are complementary to each other. While Fundamental Rights ensure freedom,
Fundamental Duties ensure responsibility.
Enjoyment of rights without duties can lead to misuse of freedom.
FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES AND DPSP
Fundamental Duties support the objectives of the Directive Principles of State Policy. Both aim to:

blocks.content: LEGAL STATUS OF FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES
Though Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, courts can use them for:

items:
• Interpreting laws
  • Determining constitutional validity
  • Promoting constitutional values

blocks.content: CONCLUSION
Fundamental Duties play a vital role in the success of democracy. They remind citizens that rights and duties go hand in hand.
A true democracy can function effectively only when citizens perform their duties sincerely and responsibly.
